title: What Is a Living Trust and Do You Really Need One?
bigPicture: A living trust lets you keep control of your assets while you’re alive and makes it easy for loved ones to receive them after you pass.
whatYouNeedToKnow: You put your house, bank accounts, or other valuables into the trust and name yourself as the boss while you’re alive.
If you become unable to make decisions, a person you trust (called a successor trustee) steps in to manage things for you.
When you die, the trust transfers your assets to the people you chose without going through court probate, which can save time and stress.
commonMistakesToAvoid: Forgetting to actually move your assets into the trust – just signing the paper isn’t enough.
Naming a successor trustee who doesn’t know your wishes or isn’t willing to act when needed.
actionSteps: Make a list of what you own and decide who should get each item after you’re gone.
Talk to an estate‑planning attorney or a trusted financial advisor to set up the trust and transfer your assets into it.
